newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lankan GDP to grow 6 pct 1997 - Bank of Ceylon.
newsitem.headline: S.Lankan GDP to grow 6 pct 1997 - Bank of Ceylon.

text.p: Sri Lanka's economy is back on track after a recent slowdown and should grow by around six percent in 1997, the state-owned Bank of Ceylon said.

The annual report from the bank's economic research division, received by Reuters on Wednesday, said higher growth would be powered by strong 10 percent year-on-year growth in the country's manufacturing sector.
Sri Lanka's gross domestic product (GDP) grew by a modest 3.8 percent in 1996, down from 5.5 percent in 1995. Manufacturing production grew by 6.5 percent last year.
The lower output last year was largely due to a severe drought, which hit agriculture and led to power cuts across the country.
The report predicted a rebound in agricultural, forestry and fishing output with year-on-year growth of 3.5 percent, against a 4.6 percent decline in 1996.
It said the Sri Lankan construction industry would grow by 5.5 percent this year, against 3.4 percent in 1996. Growth in services would remain steady at 5.8 percent, it said.
Despite the bullish forecast, the report said the 13-year-old ethnic war between the government and Tamil separatists was still hampering the country's economic development.
"The economic cost of the war is enormous and is the major impediment for the country to 'take off'," it concluded.
Government forces are battling Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels, who demand a homeland for the minority Tamil population in the north and east of the Indian Ocean island.
